features.title: Make tests/test_render.py::test_tracked_crop_actually_moves deterministic without weakening it
acceptance: Before any fix, the root cause is found and recorded in this feature's notes and in the test's docstring: which assertion failed, and why it depends on timing or load
The test passes 25 times in a row: for i in $(seq 25); do python -m pytest tests/test_render.py::test_tracked_crop_actually_moves -q || break; done
The test passes 10 times in a row while the full suite runs at the same time in another process (CPU load)
The test still asserts that early output frames are red-dominant and late frames blue-dominant
A negative-control test renders the same source with a constant crop path (cx=0.15 throughout) and shows the movement check reports 'did not move', proving the check still catches a frozen camera
The full suite still passes
features.notes: ROOT CAUSE (found before fixing): failing assertion was `assert r0 > b0` (early frame red-dominant). Cause is the test SOURCE, not timing/load and not product code: the old source passed x1=1280 to ffmpeg's `gradients` filter on a 1280-wide video, but the filter requires x1 < width, so ffmpeg replaced the out-of-range x1 with an unseeded random one. That put the red->blue crossover at x1/2, anywhere in [0,640), different on every generation (x1=1279 gives a fixed crossover at x=640); when it fell left of the 405px crop window at t=0.5s the frame was already blue. Reproduced on an idle machine: 10 of 30 freshly generated sources were bad; same render code, different source. Ruled out with evidence: OpenCV CAP_PROP_POS_MSEC seek on H.264 (seek frames pixel-identical to sequential decode at 0.5s and 9.5s) and frames at crop transitions (path is smooth, sampled frames sit mid-ramp). render.py unchanged. Fix: hue_gradient_video now builds a geq-computed ramp (one PNG, looped), identical every run (clearer fixture than relying on x1=1279); added negative control test_frozen_camera_is_reported_as_not_moved. After this merges, the lead removes the 'Known quirks' line from CLAUDE.md.

features.title: Windows compatibility: UTF-8 file I/O everywhere, guard test, and a Windows CI job
acceptance: With Python's default text encoding forced to cp1252 (simulate Windows, e.g. run a subprocess with PYTHONUTF8=0 and monkeypatched locale or by wrapping io.text_encoding), GET / returns 200 and the page contains the UTF-8 characters intact (test)

Every text-mode read_text/write_text/open in clipforge/ passes encoding='utf-8' (or is binary); tests/test_encoding.py scans the source with ast and fails on any text-mode call without an explicit encoding
A transcript, hook, note and example file containing non-ASCII text (emoji, accented letters, curly quotes) round-trips through save/load and through export_examples unchanged (test)
The rendered .ass subtitle file is written as UTF-8 so libass shows accented captions correctly (test reads the bytes)

.github/workflows/tests.yml gains a windows-latest job that installs ffmpeg and runs at least tests/test_server.py, tests/test_ui_static.py and tests/test_encoding.py (and the full suite if it passes there); the Linux job is unchanged
features.notes: Reported by Diego: localhost doesn't run on his Windows PC. Root cause found by the lead: app.py index() does (STATIC/'index.html').read_text() with no encoding; on Windows Python defaults to cp1252, and index.html contains byte 0x9D (from a right curly quote) which cp1252 can't decode -> 500 on GET /. ~20 other read_text/write_text calls have the same issue (JSON stores, .ass captions, few-shot examples). Workaround until merged: PYTHONUTF8=1. Status: code merged; Linux CI green. Windows CI fails only because windows-latest gets ffmpeg 8, which removed -vsync (ingest.py) → tracked as F22. F21 passes once the Windows job is green.

features.title: Port the useful parts of PR #2 onto main: av pin, Whisper CPU fallback that keeps the GPU, workspace header, temperature 0, raw-reply debug files
acceptance: requirements.txt pins PyAV below 19 (a line matching av<19, with a comment saying it is required by faster-whisper and why it is pinned); a test reads requirements.txt and asserts such a line exists (test in tests/test_transcribe.py)

Whisper keeps device 'auto' (GPU when available) and falls back to device='cpu' only on a missing-CUDA-library failure (RuntimeError mentioning cublas/cudnn/'Library ... not found'), at model construction OR at the first transcribe call / first iteration of the lazy segments generator; on fallback exactly one short stderr line says it fell back to CPU. Tests in tests/test_transcribe.py with a monkeypatched fake WhisperModel (no model download, no GPU): (a) fake works on auto -> used as is, no retry, no warning; (b) fake raises a CUDA-library error on auto (one case at construction, one at first transcribe/iteration) -> retried on cpu, transcript produced, warning printed; (c) an unrelated error (e.g. ValueError or a RuntimeError without CUDA-library text) propagates and is not retried

AnthropicHighlighter accepts an optional client=None constructor arg; with ANTHROPIC_WORKSPACE_ID set the anthropic client is built with default_headers {'anthropic-workspace-id': <value>}, unset -> default_headers == {}; the value is never printed or logged. Parametrized test in tests/test_highlight.py (ws set/unset) using a fake 'anthropic' module in sys.modules; existing .env.example tests in tests/test_settings.py stay green
Every highlight API call passes temperature=0; a FakeClient that records kwargs asserts temperature == 0 (test in tests/test_highlight.py)

When a chunk's reply parses to 0 clips: if the highlighter has a debug_dir, the raw reply is saved as highlight_raw_chunk_NNN.txt (utf-8) in the job dir and a stderr WARNING names the chunk index, time range and saved file name; with no debug_dir it only warns ('raw reply not saved'); a good reply saves nothing and prints nothing. Running the highlight stage via highlight_job saves the file in the job dir, a no-op rerun of the finished stage leaves it in place, and a later forced run with a good reply deletes stale highlight_raw_chunk_*.txt; stage output verification and manifest.json are unaffected by the debug files; the warning never appears in any HTTP error detail. Tests in tests/test_highlight.py (include a non-ASCII reply that round-trips byte-for-byte)

The full suite (python -m pytest tests/ -q) and python -m pyflakes clipforge tests are green; each new regression test was confirmed to fail against main's version of the file it covers (git show main:<path> or git stash) before the fix, and the builder reports which ones it checked
features.notes: Source: open PR #2 (branch step-0-windows-fixes-highlight-debug, commits a07aa97 and da57cf4) conflicts with main. The PR is a SOURCE TO READ ONLY: never merge it, never cherry-pick it, never push, never comment on/close/touch PR #2 on GitHub. Re-apply the changes by hand on a fresh local branch from main. Read the PR diff with: git diff main...origin/step-0-windows-fixes-highlight-debug. DO NOT copy the PR's Whisper change: it switched FasterWhisperTranscriber's default device from 'auto' to 'cpu' in clipforge/transcribe/backends.py, which throws away the GPU; keep 'auto' and add a targeted fallback instead (faster-whisper loads CUDA libs lazily, so the error may only appear when the segments generator is first iterated; make sure the retry re-runs transcription from the start on cpu and does not emit duplicate segments). PR implementation shape worth keeping: RAW_REPLY_NAME / RAW_REPLY_GLOB constants in clipforge/highlight/backends.py, a 'debug_dir: Path | None = None' attribute on the Highlighter base class, set by highlight_job in clipforge/highlight/run.py, which deletes stale highlight_raw_chunk_*.txt only before a run that actually executes (forced or not yet done), never on a no-op rerun. Debug warnings are CLI/server-side stderr logging only (LESSONS.md: no paths or job ids in HTTP error details). ANTHROPIC_WORKSPACE_ID is not CLIPFORGE_-prefixed, so the F01 .env.example check does not require it; document it anyway and never print its value. Tests must never call the real Claude API or download models. SKIP (already on main via F21/F22/F02; do not re-add): encoding='utf-8' on read_text/write_text and load_examples, CLI stdout/stderr UTF-8 reconfigure, ffmpeg filter-path escaping, -fps_mode replacing -vsync, test_render fixture changes, and the CLAUDE.md note about the flaky render test. Optional follow-up: strip whitespace-only ANTHROPIC_WORKSPACE_ID. Bug reported on Windows with anthropic 1.13.0: TypeError: Messages.create() got an unexpected keyword argument 'temperature'. The lead checked the repo venv: anthropic 1.13.0 is installed, and inspect.signature(anthropic.resources.messages.Messages.create) has NO temperature but DOES have workspace_id (also max_tokens, messages, model, system, extra_headers, ...). The builder should check these facts again with .venv/bin/python -I before coding. Must be built and merged BEFORE F10, which also touches clipforge/highlight/backends.py. Do not touch PR #2 or any of F10's files except clipforge/highlight/backends.py. The F23 debug/raw-reply code (RAW_REPLY_NAME/RAW_REPLY_GLOB, debug_dir, stale-file cleanup) stays as is. acceptance: There is one editable data file per platform: tiktok, reels, shorts, x and facebook. Each has max length, target length range, output size 1080x1920, a caption safe-zone rectangle and a tier (main for tiktok/reels/shorts, side for x/facebook). A test loads all 5

Asking for an unknown platform raises a clear error listing the valid names (test)

A helper returns the safe zone shared by all main-tier platforms. It is a non-empty rectangle inside 1080x1920, and changing one profile file's safe zone changes the result (test with temp profile files)

Someone with web access must verify limits and safe zones against the official platform help pages and set real YYYY-MM-DD dates + source URLs before relying on the numbers. features.title: Smarter highlight picking: trigger/peak/payoff times, context setup, hook type, stranger check
acceptance: The highlight system prompt asks for trigger_t, reaction_peak_t, payoff_end_t, context_setup (one line), hook_type (fixed vocabulary) and a stranger check, and says moments that need backstory must be rejected. A test checks each field name appears in the built prompt

parse_llm_response keeps valid new fields. Times that are out of order or outside [start, end] are cleared (the candidate is kept). An unknown hook_type becomes 'other'. A multi-line context_setup is cut to one line (tests with crafted LLM text)
A candidate whose stranger check fails is left out of candidates and listed in CandidateSet.rejected with its reason (test)
A v1 candidates.json fixture without the new fields still loads, and the refine/render tests pass unchanged (test)
MockHighlighter fills every new field deterministically, so a mock pipeline run gives candidates.json entries with trigger_t <= reaction_peak_t <= payoff_end_t inside each clip (test)

features.title: Hook-first trimming and a first-3-seconds hook score
acceptance: For a candidate with trigger_t well after its start (a preamble), the refined clip's first spoken sentence is the one containing trigger_t, and the clip's end is not before payoff_end_t. The no-word-straddles-a-cut invariant and the length limits still hold (test with a crafted transcript)

When cutting the preamble would make the clip too short or break limits, the original start is kept and the reason is recorded. Candidates without trigger_t refine exactly as before, and the existing refine tests pass unchanged

Every rendered clip's report has hook_score: a 0-100 total plus four sub-scores (speech in second 1, motion in second 1, face visible, on-screen text in the first 3 s), each with a one-line reason (mock pipeline test)

Sub-scores respond to their signals: first word at 0.2 s scores higher speech than first word at 2.5 s; a moving testsrc scores higher motion than a static color clip; a scripted MockDetector face gives a full face score and no face gives 0; captions disabled with no overlay gives text score 0 (tests with synthetic inputs)
features.notes: Follow-ups: when the payoff would be lost, _hook_first keeps the original start but _enforce_length can still cut the payoff (trim anyway or reject); get_detector is built on every run_pipeline call even when all clips already have a hook_score; motion score counts burned-in caption changes; weights (speech 30/motion 20/face 25/text 25) are uncalibrated; the F12 overlay span is wired into the text score by F12.
